# Complete the default DockLayout action rail in Workstation

## Context

Epic #17836 is the greenfield DockLayouts authority. The pane-header family shipped through individually gated leaves (`#17947`, `#17948`, `#17950`, `#17951`, `#17963`), but the operator acceptance bar was never delivered as one product contract: every DockLayout tabs node uses inline chrome; overflow is first when active; `reload · pin · pop-out · maximize` occupy the focus-gated middle rail; close is persistent and last; the flagship proves every action and its visual language.

The goal-recovery matrix is recorded at [Epic comment 5491147214](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/17836#issuecomment-5491147214). Euclid's cross-family convergence review is [comment 5491304086](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/17836#issuecomment-5491304086). Vega independently mapped the Workstation lifecycle/cache constraints and self-selected that surface. This body folds both peer reviews into one successor rather than creating a second ticket.

Live source was revalidated at `dev@bd463173f2`; the relevant files are unchanged from the measured current-dev Workstation run.

## The Problem

The implementation optimised every leaf for byte-identical-off adoption:

- `DockWorkspace` defaults `enableDockCloseAction`, `enableDockPinAction`, `enableDockReloadAction`, `enableDockMaximizeAction`, and `enableDockPopOutAction` to `false`;
- `LayoutAdapter` owns the correct frozen ordering, but projects only the subset a consumer explicitly enabled;
- Workstation enables only close, pin, and maximize;
- Workstation has no `resolveFreshPane` contract and its `paneCache` has no post-commit adoption seam;
- Workstation owns a mature custom `tearOutHandlers` lifecycle while the base pop-out action is gated by a separate `enableDockTearOutLifecycle` construction path;
- the flagship E2E asserts overflow-first and close-last, so an empty middle rail still passes.

This is the exact leaf-green/product-incomplete failure the recovery is correcting. The five action flags remain public opt-outs, but their product default must be the complete rail.

### Rail round-trip acceptance correction

Operator screenshots on current Workstation state expose two product defects in the pin round-trip:

- The reveal overlay's restore control inherits the default primary Button UI, producing an oversized blue `Pin` CTA inside pane chrome.
- Railing the final live item of a tabs child inside an edge-band split leaves that empty tab container and its close action rendered. Closed #15837 removed direct empty tabs bands but explicitly preserved split bands; this is the nested tail of that exemption.


## The Architectural Reality

### Default rail

- `src/dashboard/dock/projection/LayoutAdapter.mjs#resolveTabConfig` already owns the stable node-level action array and frozen order.
- `Neo.tab.plugin.Overflow` contributes independently through `projectAsAction: true`; it must remain first only while overflow exists and must never enter the tab collection.
- Middle actions inherit `TabContainer`'s `showOnFocus` / reactive `containsFocus` contract. Stable action instances change state without replacing the array. #18015 makes focus-inactive actions occupy zero space and excludes collapsed actions from Overflow measurement. Focus may legitimately repartition direct tabs versus the overflow menu.
- `close` is the deliberate exception: persistent, `contextual: false`, and last.
- `lock` is outside the operator goal and remains opt-in.

### Reload / cache ownership

- Merged #17996 already routes reload to `dockReload()` when present and otherwise to the two-phase recreate transaction.
- `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs#resolvePane` is cache-backed and owns pane constructors plus shared Provider/Store injection.
- Workstation's root Provider owns shared Store instances. A generic per-pane “reload the store” default would refresh multiple panes behind a pane-local affordance. Workstation therefore requires an explicit fresh-pane contract; persisted blueprint/store reload is not an honest fallback.
- `resolveFreshPane` cannot update `paneCache` during prepare. A failed insert would leave the old pane live while the cache pointed at an uncommitted candidate.
- Successful commit needs one post-commit acknowledgement (hook or committed-pane result): candidate is live, cache adopts that exact pane, then the predecessor retires. Refusal/throw leaves slot and cache identities unchanged.

### Pop-out / lifecycle ownership

- Workstation already owns one proven tear-out handler bundle, vessel embodiment, park owners, connection admission, and a custom `onDockTearOutExit`.
- Enabling base `enableDockTearOutLifecycle` merely to satisfy `dockPopOutActionActive` would construct a second handler/listener lifecycle.
- Pop-out capability must derive from the one effective host handler/admission bundle. A header click enters the exact same exit → terminal → retire/reintegrate path as the pointer gesture.

## The Fix

### 1. Consume #18015's focus-geometry prerequisite

#18015 owns generic toolbar flow and collapsed-action exclusion from Overflow measurement. This ticket proves that landed behavior in Workstation; it does not duplicate the algorithm.

### 2. Make the five action flags default-on

Keep these public configs as explicit opt-outs, but default them to `true`:

- `enableDockCloseAction`
- `enableDockPinAction`
- `enableDockReloadAction`
- `enableDockPopOutAction`
- `enableDockMaximizeAction`

Keep `enableDockLockAction` default-off.

Every DockWorkspace projects stable engine identities in this order:

`overflow → reload → pin → pop-out → maximize → close`

Overflow remains plugin-owned and conditional on actual overflow. Capability/policy changes state, never list membership. Close remains persistent/last; inactive middle actions occupy zero space, and focus may repartition tabs versus the overflow menu without changing action membership or the active-tab invariant.

### 3. Close the rail round-trip tails

- Give the reveal overlay's pin/restore affordance a compact non-primary Button treatment through the shared component seam; do not patch only Workstation.
- During split projection, omit child tab flows with zero live items after railing. Rebuild splitters only between surviving children; an all-empty split makes the owning edge band rail-only. The committed split/tree stays unchanged and returns intact when an item is restored.

### 4. Complete Workstation reload

- Factor Workstation's cache-miss pane construction into one fresh-candidate factory that does not consult or mutate `paneCache`.
- `resolvePane` uses it only on cache miss; `resolveFreshPane` always creates independently.
- Add the narrow post-commit adoption seam needed to swap `paneCache[itemId]` only after the exact candidate is live.
- Delegation retains priority where a pane implements `dockReload()`; contract-less panes recreate.

### 5. Complete Workstation pop-out

- Make action availability derive from Workstation's existing effective handler bundle.
- Reuse the exact current handler identity and custom exit seam; do not create another lifecycle or listener set.
- The action measures the live pane and enters the existing pointer tear-out terminal path.

### 6. Close on one flagship acceptance artifact

Extend the existing Workstation acceptance surface with multiple independent real-click arms—not one order-dependent pane screenplay:

- exact ordered vector on every projected tabs node;
- focus reveals the stable middle rail from zero inactive extent without changing action membership; direct tabs may repartition against overflow while the active tab remains directly visible;
- reload proves delegation and contract-less recreate on different panes;
- pin proves rail transition and reversible reveal;
- pop-out proves existing vessel admission and same-pane identity;
- maximize proves measured workspace geometry and restore;
- four Engine themes plus Workstation's custom palette produce computed-style receipts;
- operator screenshot acceptance gates goal closure.

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0029 §§2.1, 2.6, and 2.8 and Epic #17836's greenfield/no-compatibility authority`. No persisted schema or wire change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `enableDockCloseAction`, `enableDockPinAction`, `enableDockReloadAction`, `enableDockPopOutAction`, and `enableDockMaximizeAction` default to `true` and retain explicit `false` opt-out; `enableDockLockAction` remains default-off.
- [ ] Every default DockWorkspace projects stable action identities ordered `reload · pin · pop-out · maximize · close`; overflow is the first action only while overflowing, and remains outside the tab collection.
- [ ] Close is persistent/last. The four middle actions use `showOnFocus`, have zero main-axis extent while context-inactive, and reveal without replacing/reordering actions; direct tabs may repartition against overflow while the active tab stays directly visible.
- [ ] Reload/pin/pop-out capability or item-policy changes update stable instances through state. Host action ordering and generic non-dock tab behavior remain unchanged.
- [ ] The reveal overlay pin control uses a compact non-primary treatment in all four Engine themes and Workstation palettes; enabled and disabled states remain legible.
- [ ] Railing the last live item from one split child removes that empty tabs shell and its orphan actions; surviving children fill the split, all-empty splits yield rail-only, and restoring an item reconstructs the committed split geometry.
- [ ] Workstation's fresh-pane factory bypasses `paneCache`; `resolvePane` uses it only on cache miss and `resolveFreshPane` always creates independently.
- [ ] Successful recreate adopts the exact committed pane in `paneCache` only after it is live; every refusal/throw preserves the exact predecessor, slot, cache entry, and document. Delegation retains priority.
- [ ] Workstation pop-out uses the exact existing `tearOutHandlers` identity and custom exit/terminal path; no second handler/listener/vessel owner is created.
- [ ] Header-action pop-out opens/adopts a vessel at the measured pane rect, and existing retire/reintegration behavior returns the same live pane where required. Refusal commits nothing.
- [ ] One existing Workstation acceptance artifact asserts the ordered vector for every tabs node and independently clicks reload, pin, pop-out, and maximize through production paths.
- [ ] That artifact proves no inactive-action gap, focus-time repartition preserves the active-tab/overflow invariants, no duplicate action owner, and no action/tab contamination.
- [ ] All four Engine themes plus Workstation's custom light/dark palette have computed-style and screenshot evidence. Operator visual acceptance is required before the Epic goal row closes.
- [ ] Exact-head unit, component, and targeted Workstation E2E suites are green; mutation controls prove the default vector, cache adoption, and lifecycle-owner arms red when reverted.

## Out of Scope

- Making lock part of the default engine set.
- New action names, new action semantics, or a new focus system.
- Generic `showOnFocus` flow and collapsed-action exclusion from Overflow measurement (#18015).
- Restyling inline tabs/header actions; #17950/#17963 own the shipped chrome/value layer.
- A second reload or tear-out lifecycle.
- Per-pane Store topology changes.
- Persisting reload/maximize/action state.
- Updating external consumer repositories in this PR.

## Avoided Traps

- **Delete the public flags.** That is an API break not required by the operator goal; default-on plus explicit opt-out delivers the product without forcing every consumer.
- **Another per-app opt-in patch.** It fixes one screenshot and leaves the framework default wrong.
- **Generic data reload.** Shared Store instances turn a pane-local affordance into a multi-pane refresh.
- **Mutate `paneCache` during prepare.** Failed commit would split live slot and cache truth.
- **Enable the base tear-out lifecycle beside Workstation's bundle.** Two handlers/listener sets violate single ownership.
- **Vary action arrays per active item.** Retained toolbar identity and overflow projection would race again.
- **One sequential all-action screenplay.** Pin/pop-out intentionally move panes; independent arms in one flagship artifact test contracts rather than choreography order.
- **Fixture transfer.** Dedicated fixtures do not prove Workstation wiring or operator-visible quality.
